records.source: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יְהֽוֹשָׁפָט֙ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר עִם־אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑יד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ יְהוֹרָ֥ם בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And lay down Jehoshaphat with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in [the] city of David, and reigned Jehoram his son in his place.
pieces: Then Jehoshaphat rested with his ancestors and was buried with them in the City of David. His son Jehoram became king in his place.

L.1: And Jehoshaphat lay down with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the City of David, and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

R.1: Then Jehoshaphat died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Jehoram became king after him.

decisions.choice: the close of 1 Kings 22:51, almost word for word
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 1 Kings 22:51, which ends Jehoshaphat's reign in Kings. The only difference is that Kings says "the City of David his father"; Chronicles says "the City of David". Chronicles ends Jehoshaphat's story at 20:37 and begins Jehoram's reign here.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The death formula, as at 12:16 and 1 Kings 22:51: he died and joined his ancestors. Here the Hebrew also names his burial with them.

decisions.choice: Jehoram: Jehoshaphat's son, also called Joram
decisions.reason: Jehoram is the full form of the name; 2 Kings 8:21-24 also calls him Joram. A king of Israel of the same name, Joram son of Ahab, reigned at the same time (2 Kings 8:16).

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died
decisions.reason: The death formula as worded throughout Kings and Chronicles; Readable adds "was buried with his ancestors" where the Hebrew names the burial. The wording of 1 Kings 22:51 is kept.

records.heading: Jehoram king of Judah

records.source: וְלֽוֹ־אַחִ֞ים בְּנֵ֣י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֗ט עֲזַרְיָ֤ה וִֽיחִיאֵל֙ וּזְכַרְיָ֣הוּ וַעֲזַרְיָ֔הוּ וּמִיכָאֵ֖ל וּשְׁפַטְיָ֑הוּ כָּל־אֵ֕לֶּה בְּנֵ֥י יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֥לֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And to him [were] brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah and Jehiel and Zechariah and Azariah and Michael and Shephatiah; all these [were] sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
pieces: He had brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

L.2: And he had brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah and Jehiel and Zechariah and Azariah and Michael and Shephatiah; all these [were] sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

R.2: Jehoram had six brothers, the other sons of Jehoshaphat. Their names were Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael and Shephatiah. All of them were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.

decisions.choice: two brothers named Azariah
decisions.reason: The first and fourth names are two forms of the same name, Azariah ("Yahweh has helped"): a short form and a longer form ending in -yahu. Two sons of one father may have shared a name in its two forms, or one form may have come in by a copying slip. The list keeps both.

decisions.choice: king of Israel: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, as king of the people of Israel
decisions.reason: Jehoshaphat ruled Judah. Chronicles often calls Judah and its people "Israel", since they are the true continuation of the people of God (12:1, 6; 21:4). Some ancient Greek and Syriac copies and a few Hebrew manuscripts read "king of Judah", which may be an easing of the harder reading.

decisions.choice: to him were brothers: Jehoram had brothers
decisions.reason: Hebrew says "to him were" for "he had". The list prepares for verse 4, where Jehoram kills them.

decisions.choice: six brothers, the other sons
decisions.reason: Readable gives the number of names in the list and says "other" so that Jehoram himself is not taken for one of the six. Readable also gives the list its own sentence.

records.source: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֣ם׀אֲ֠בִיהֶם מַתָּנ֨וֹת רַבּ֜וֹת לְכֶ֤סֶף וּלְזָהָב֙ וּלְמִגְדָּנ֔וֹת עִם־עָרֵ֥י מְצֻר֖וֹת בִּֽיהוּדָ֑ה וְאֶת־הַמַּמְלָכָ֛ה נָתַ֥ן לִֽיהוֹרָ֖ם כִּי־ה֥וּא הַבְּכֽוֹר׃פ
records.gloss: And gave to them their father gifts many of silver and of gold and of precious things, with cities fortified in Judah; but the kingdom he gave to Jehoram, for he [was] the firstborn.
pieces: Their father had given them many gifts of silver, gold and valuable things, together with fortified cities in Judah; the kingdom, however, he gave to Jehoram, since Jehoram was the firstborn.

L.3: And their father gave them many gifts of silver and of gold and of precious things, with fortified cities in Judah; but the kingdom he gave to Jehoram, for he [was] the firstborn.

R.3: Their father had given each of them rich gifts: silver, gold and other valuable things. He also gave them strong, walled cities in Judah. But he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because Jehoram was his oldest son.

decisions.choice: gave: had given, during Jehoshaphat's life
decisions.reason: The verb continues the account, but what it tells happened before Jehoshaphat's death in verse 1: it is background to Jehoram's murders in verse 4.

decisions.choice: precious things: costly gifts
decisions.reason: The word names choice and valuable goods, as in Genesis 24:53 and Ezra 1:6.

decisions.choice: gifts and cities for the younger sons, the throne for the firstborn
decisions.reason: Rehoboam did the same for his sons (11:23): the younger sons were given wealth and posts in the fortified cities, which provided for them and kept them away from the capital. The kingdom went to the firstborn, as was the custom, though a king could choose otherwise (1 Kings 1:17; 2 Chronicles 11:22).

decisions.choice: had given (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "had given" to show that the gifts came before the events of verse 4 (m1).

decisions.choice: strong, walled cities; oldest son
decisions.reason: Readable says what a fortified city was and what "firstborn" means.

records.source: וַיָּ֨קָם יְהוֹרָ֜ם עַל־מַמְלֶ֤כַת אָבִיו֙ וַיִּתְחַזַּ֔ק וַיַּהֲרֹ֥ג אֶת־כָּל־אֶחָ֖יו בֶּחָ֑רֶב וְגַ֖ם מִשָּׂרֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And arose Jehoram over [the] kingdom of his father and strengthened himself, and killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of [the] princes of Israel.
pieces: When Jehoram had taken over his father's kingdom and made himself secure, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and some of the officials of Israel as well.

L.4: And Jehoram rose up over the kingdom of his father and made himself strong, and he killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Israel.

R.4: Jehoram took his father's place as king. Once his power was secure, he killed all his brothers with the sword. He also killed some of Israel's leaders.

decisions.choice: rose up over the kingdom: took control of the kingdom
decisions.reason: To rise up over a kingdom is to take one's place as its ruler.

decisions.choice: strengthened himself: made his hold on power secure
decisions.reason: The same verb is used of Solomon (1:1) and Rehoboam (12:13) when they were firmly in control. Here it leads straight into murder: once secure, Jehoram removed every rival.

decisions.choice: killing his brothers: removing rivals for the throne
decisions.reason: Brothers and leading men who might back them were possible claimants to the throne. Jehoram's murders are told only in Chronicles; Elijah's letter names them as a reason for judgment (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the princes of Israel: leaders in Judah
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, "Israel" here means the people Jehoram ruled in Judah, not the northern kingdom.

decisions.choice: princes / officials / leaders
decisions.reason: As set for these books for sar.

records.source: בֶּן־שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה יְהוֹרָ֣ם בְּמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁמוֹנֶ֣ה שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: A son of thirty and two year[s] [was] Jehoram when he became king, and eight years he reigned in Jerusalem.
pieces: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

L.5: Jehoram [was] a son of thirty-two years when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

R.5: Jehoram became king at the age of thirty-two, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eight years.

decisions.choice: the accession formula of 2 Kings 8:17
decisions.reason: Verses 5-10 follow 2 Kings 8:17-22. This verse is the same as 2 Kings 8:17, except that it names Jehoram where Kings says "he was". It is repeated in verse 20.

decisions.choice: a son of thirty-two years: thirty-two years old
decisions.reason: Hebrew gives a person's age as being "a son of" so many years.

decisions.choice: the wording of 2 Kings 8:17
decisions.reason: The wording of the accession formula in 2 Kings 8:17 is kept at each level, with Jehoram's name where Chronicles has it.

records.source: וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ׀מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֔ב כִּ֚י בַּת־אַחְאָ֔ב הָ֥יְתָה לּ֖וֹ אִשָּׁ֑ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he walked in [the] way of [the] kings of Israel, as had done [the] house of Ahab, for [the] daughter of Ahab was to him [as] wife; and he did the evil in [the] eyes of Yahweh.
pieces: He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for he had married Ahab's daughter. He did what was evil in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.6: And he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for the daughter of Ahab was his wife; and he did the evil in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.6: He lived the way the kings of Israel had lived, just as Ahab's family had done, because his wife was Ahab's daughter. He did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said was evil.

decisions.choice: the same as 2 Kings 8:18
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 2 Kings 8:18 with no change in meaning.

decisions.choice: walked in the way of the kings of Israel: followed the worship of the north
decisions.reason: To walk in a way is to live by it. Judah's king takes up the ways of the northern kings and of Ahab's house in particular, with its worship of Baal (1 Kings 16:31-33). Verses 11-13 say what this meant in Judah.

decisions.choice: the daughter of Ahab: Athaliah
decisions.reason: 22:2 names her as Athaliah. The marriage sealed Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahab (18:1).

decisions.choice: did the evil in [the] eyes of / did what was evil in the sight of / did what the LORD said was evil
decisions.reason: The verdict formula, worded the same way at each level throughout Kings and Chronicles; the wording of 2 Kings 8:18 is kept.

records.source: וְלֹא־אָבָ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה לְהַשְׁחִית֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית דָּוִ֔יד לְמַ֣עַן הַבְּרִ֔ית אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖ת לְדָוִ֑יד וְכַאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֗ר לָתֵ֨ת ל֥וֹ נִ֛יר וּלְבָנָ֖יו כָּל־הַיָּמִֽים׃
records.gloss: But not was willing Yahweh to destroy the house of David, for [the] sake of the covenant that he had made with David, and as he had said to give to him a lamp and to his sons all the days.
pieces: Yet {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not willing to destroy the house of David, for the sake of the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made with David, since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised to give a lamp to him and to his descendants for all time.

L.7: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was not willing to destroy the house of David, for the sake of the covenant that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made with David, and as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised to give a lamp to him and to his sons all the days.

R.7: But {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did not want to destroy David's family, because of the covenant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made with David. He had promised David that one of his descendants would always rule, like a lamp that keeps burning.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 8:19 with three differences
decisions.reason: Kings says Yahweh was not willing to destroy "Judah"; Chronicles says "the house of David". Kings says "for the sake of David his servant"; Chronicles says "for the sake of the covenant that he had made with David". Kings has "a lamp for his sons"; Chronicles has "a lamp to him and to his sons". Chronicles puts the weight on the royal line and on Yahweh's covenant with it.

decisions.choice: the covenant made with David: Yahweh's promise of a lasting line
decisions.reason: The promise of 2 Samuel 7:12-16 (1 Chronicles 17:11-14) is called a covenant here, as in 13:5 and Psalm 89:4. Jehoram's sin deserved the end of his house, but the covenant held.

decisions.choice: a lamp: a line of David's descendants that does not die out
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 8:19 and 1 Kings 11:36, a lamp left burning in a house is a sign that the family lives on: a son of David on the throne in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: descendants; for all time (Balanced); always (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 8:19: Balanced and Readable say "descendants" for "sons", since the line runs on for generations.

decisions.choice: one of his descendants would always rule, like a lamp that keeps burning
decisions.reason: Readable says what the lamp stands for and keeps the picture as a comparison, as at 2 Kings 8:19. It also says "David's family" for "the house of David".

records.source: בְּיָמָיו֙ פָּשַׁ֣ע אֱד֔וֹם מִתַּ֖חַת יַד־יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: In his days rebelled Edom from under [the] hand of Judah, and they made king over themselves a king.
pieces: During his reign Edom rebelled against the rule of Judah and set up a king of its own.

L.8: In his days Edom rebelled from under the hand of Judah, and they made a king over themselves.

R.8: While Jehoram was king, the Edomites rebelled against Judah's rule and made one of their own men king.

decisions.choice: the same as 2 Kings 8:20
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 2 Kings 8:20 word for word.

decisions.choice: Edom: the land south-east of Judah, ruled by Judah until now
decisions.reason: Edom had been subject to Judah since David's time (1 Chronicles 18:13). In Jehoshaphat's day it had only a deputy for a king (1 Kings 22:48). Now it breaks free.

decisions.choice: from under the hand of Judah: from Judah's control
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for power, and to be under someone's hand is to be ruled by him.

decisions.choice: against the rule of Judah (Balanced); against Judah's rule (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 8:20, Balanced and Readable say what "from under the hand" means (m3).

records.source: וַיַּֽעֲבֹ֤ר יְהוֹרָם֙ עִם־שָׂרָ֔יו וְכָל־הָרֶ֖כֶב עִמּ֑וֹ וַיְהִי֙ קָ֣ם לַ֔יְלָה וַיַּ֗ךְ אֶת־אֱדוֹם֙ הַסּוֹבֵ֣ב אֵלָ֔יו וְאֵ֖ת שָׂרֵ֥י הָרָֽכֶב׃
records.gloss: And crossed over Jehoram with his commanders, and all the chariots with him; and it was, he arose by night and struck Edom, the [one] surrounding him, and [the] commanders of the chariots.
pieces: So Jehoram crossed over with his commanders and all his chariots. He rose by night and attacked the Edomites who had surrounded him and the chariot commanders.

L.9: And Jehoram crossed over with his commanders, and all the chariots with him. And it happened [that] he arose by night and struck Edom, which was surrounding him, and the commanders of the chariots.

R.9: So Jehoram marched out with his commanders and all his chariots. The Edomites surrounded him, but he got up during the night and attacked them and the chariot commanders.

decisions.choice: with his commanders, where 2 Kings 8:21 has "to Zair"
decisions.reason: Kings says Joram crossed over "to Zair"; Chronicles says Jehoram crossed over "with his commanders". The two phrases look alike in Hebrew writing, so one may have come from the other in copying. Chronicles also leaves out the end of 2 Kings 8:21, "and the people fled to their tents", and calls the king Jehoram where Kings has Joram.

decisions.choice: he struck Edom who surrounded him: Jehoram broke out of an encirclement
decisions.reason: As in 2 Kings 8:21, the sense seems to be that the Edomites had surrounded Jehoram's force and that he broke out by night, striking them and their chariot commanders. Verse 10 shows that the campaign still failed: Edom stayed free.

decisions.choice: commanders: Judah's officers in verse 9a, Edom's in 9b
decisions.reason: The same word is used twice: first for Jehoram's own commanders, then for the commanders of the chariots he attacked, who belonged to Edom.

decisions.choice: marched out
decisions.reason: Readable says "marched out" for "crossed over", since Chronicles does not name the place he crossed to, and gives the Edomite attack first so the order of events is clear.

records.source: וַיִּפְשַׁ֨ע אֱד֜וֹם מִתַּ֣חַת יַד־יְהוּדָ֗ה עַ֚ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֔ה אָ֣ז תִּפְשַׁ֥ע לִבְנָ֛ה בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִ֖יא מִתַּ֣חַת יָד֑וֹ כִּ֣י עָזַ֔ב אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י אֲבֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And rebelled Edom from under [the] hand of Judah until the day the this; then rebelled Libnah at the time the that from under his hand, for he had forsaken Yahweh [the] God of his fathers.
pieces: So Edom has been in rebellion against the rule of Judah to this day. Libnah also rebelled against his rule at that same time, because he had forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of his ancestors.

L.10: And Edom has rebelled from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah rebelled at that time from under his hand, because he had forsaken {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of his fathers.

R.10: So Edom has stayed free from Judah's rule to this day. At the same time the town of Libnah also rebelled against Jehoram's rule. This happened because he had turned away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of his ancestors.

decisions.choice: 2 Kings 8:22 with a reason added
decisions.reason: The verse repeats 2 Kings 8:22 and adds two things: Libnah rebelled "from under his hand", and it happened "because he had forsaken Yahweh the God of his fathers". Chronicles often names the reason for a king's losses (12:2; 24:24).

decisions.choice: because he had forsaken Yahweh: the reason for both revolts
alternatives: the reason for Libnah's revolt only
decisions.reason: The reason stands after Libnah's revolt, but it explains Jehoram's losses as a whole, Edom's revolt as well as Libnah's.

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own day
decisions.reason: As at 5:9, "to this day" means the time when the account was written, here repeated from 2 Kings 8:22.

decisions.choice: Libnah: a town in the lowland of Judah
decisions.reason: Libnah lay in the low hills west of Judah, near the Philistine border, and was a town of the priests (Joshua 21:13; 1 Chronicles 6:42). Its revolt shows Judah losing ground on the west as well as in Edom.

decisions.choice: has been in rebellion (Balanced); has stayed free (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 2 Kings 8:22: "to this day" makes the revolt a lasting state. Balanced says "ancestors" for "fathers".

decisions.choice: turned away from
decisions.reason: Readable says "turned away from" for "forsaken", a less common word, and gives the reason its own sentence.

records.source: גַּם־ה֥וּא עָשָֽׂה־בָמ֖וֹת בְּהָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֶּ֨זֶן֙ אֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וַיַּדַּ֖ח אֶת־יְהוּדָֽה׃פ
records.gloss: Also he made high places in [the] mountains of Judah, and he made prostitute [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, and he drove astray Judah.
pieces: He also made high places in the hill country of Judah. He caused the people of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves and led Judah astray.

L.11: He also made high places in the mountains of Judah, and he caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves, and he drove Judah astray.

R.11: He also built hilltop shrines in the hill country of Judah. He led the people of Jerusalem to be unfaithful to God, like a wife who sleeps with other men, and he made Judah turn away from God.

decisions.choice: high places: local shrines
decisions.reason: High places were places of worship, often on hills, outside the temple in Jerusalem. Jehoshaphat had removed them (17:6); his son set them up again. Verses 11-20 have no parallel in Kings.

decisions.choice: caused them to prostitute themselves: led them to worship other gods
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the language of prostitution for Israel's unfaithfulness to Yahweh, who is pictured as her husband (Exodus 34:15-16; Deuteronomy 31:16; Hosea 1:2). The worship at the high places, after Ahab's example (verse 13), broke faith with him.

decisions.choice: drove astray: pushed away from Yahweh
decisions.reason: The verb means to push or drive someone away, here from the right way, as in Deuteronomy 13:6, 11, where it is used of those who lead others to serve other gods.

decisions.choice: in the mountains of Judah
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek and Latin translations read "in the cities of Judah"; the two words differ by one letter in Hebrew. The meaning is close: shrines throughout Judah.

decisions.choice: high places / high places / hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: As set for these books for bamot.

decisions.choice: to be unfaithful to God, like a wife who sleeps with other men; turn away from God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of prostitution as unfaithfulness in a marriage (m2) and names God as the one Judah left.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א אֵלָיו֙ מִכְתָּ֔ב מֵֽאֵלִיָּ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹ֑ר כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֔יךָ תַּ֗חַת אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־הָלַ֨כְתָּ֙ בְּדַרְכֵי֙ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֣ט אָבִ֔יךָ וּבְדַרְכֵ֖י אָסָ֥א מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָֽה׃
records.gloss: And came to him a writing from Elijah the prophet saying, Thus says Yahweh [the] God of David your father: Because that not you have walked in [the] ways of Jehoshaphat your father and in [the] ways of Asa king of Judah,
pieces: Then a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, which said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} the God of your ancestor David says this: Because you have not followed the ways of your father Jehoshaphat, nor the ways of Asa king of Judah,

L.12: And a letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of David your father: Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

R.12: Then a letter came to Jehoram from Elijah the prophet. It said, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your ancestor David, says: You have not lived the way your father Jehoshaphat lived, or the way Asa king of Judah lived.

decisions.choice: a letter from Elijah the prophet
decisions.reason: The word means a written document. This is the only time Elijah is named in Chronicles and the only written message of his in Scripture. It brings Yahweh's word in the prophet's usual form, "Thus says Yahweh".

decisions.choice: when the letter came: Elijah's place in the time of Jehoram
alternatives: Elijah was still alive in Jehoram's early years
Elijah wrote the letter before he was taken up, to be delivered later
decisions.reason: 2 Kings 2 tells of Elijah's being taken up before the events of 2 Kings 3, which are set while Jehoshaphat was still alive (2 Kings 3:7, 11). So Elijah may have been gone before Jehoram became king. But the accounts of Kings are not always told in time order, and Jehoram reigned for a time beside his father (2 Kings 1:17; 8:16), so Elijah may still have been alive early in his reign. Others suggest that Elijah wrote the letter before he was taken up, for it to be delivered later. The text does not say.

decisions.choice: David your father: your ancestor David
decisions.reason: "Father" here means forefather. Jehoshaphat, named next, is his father in the ordinary sense.

decisions.choice: the ways of Jehoshaphat and Asa: the faithful kings before him
decisions.reason: Jehoshaphat and Asa are judged in Chronicles as kings who sought Yahweh (14:1; 17:3-4), though not without fault. Jehoram broke with their example.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD / The LORD ... says this / This is what the LORD ... says
decisions.reason: The prophetic formula as worded at each level in these books.

decisions.choice: a statement in its own sentence
decisions.reason: Readable drops "because" and makes the charge a sentence of its own; verse 14 then gives the result with "So".

records.heading: Elijah's letter

records.source: וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּדֶ֨רֶךְ֙ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַתַּזְנֶ֤ה אֶת־יְהוּדָה֙ וְאֶת־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם כְּהַזְנ֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב וְגַ֨ם אֶת־אַחֶ֧יךָ בֵית־אָבִ֛יךָ הַטּוֹבִ֥ים מִמְּךָ֖ הָרָֽגְתָּ׃
records.gloss: and you have walked in [the] way of [the] kings of Israel, and made prostitute Judah and [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem like [the] prostituting of [the] house of Ahab, and also your brothers, [the] house of your father, the good [ones] more than you, you have killed,
pieces: but have followed the way of the kings of Israel, and have led Judah and the people of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves, as the house of Ahab did, and have also killed your brothers, your own father's family, men better than you,

L.13: but you have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have caused Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to prostitute themselves, like the prostituting of the house of Ahab, and you have also killed your brothers, your father's house, who were better than you,

R.13: Instead, you have lived the way the kings of Israel lived. You have led Judah and the people of Jerusalem to be unfaithful to God, just as Ahab's family led Israel to be unfaithful. You have even killed your own brothers, your father's sons, who were better men than you.

decisions.choice: caused them to prostitute themselves: led them to worship other gods
decisions.reason: As in verse 11.

decisions.choice: the prostituting of the house of Ahab: the worship of Baal
decisions.reason: Ahab and Jezebel led Israel to worship Baal and Asherah (1 Kings 16:31-33; 21:25-26). Jehoram brought the same into Judah.

decisions.choice: your brothers, your father's house: the brothers are the father's family
decisions.reason: "Your father's house" stands beside "your brothers" and names the same people: the sons of Jehoshaphat killed in verse 4. They were "better" than Jehoram in that they were more righteous than he was.

decisions.choice: men better than you (Balanced); better men than you (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "men" for the plural adjective "the good ones", since the brothers are meant.

decisions.choice: led Israel to be unfaithful
decisions.reason: Readable says what the house of Ahab did, to make the comparison clear.

records.source: הִנֵּ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה נֹגֵ֛ף מַגֵּפָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה בְּעַמֶּ֑ךָ וּבְבָנֶ֥יךָ וּבְנָשֶׁ֖יךָ וּבְכָל־רְכוּשֶֽׁךָ׃
records.gloss: look, Yahweh [is] striking a blow great on your people and on your sons and on your wives and on all your possessions,
pieces: so now {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to bring a heavy blow on your people, on your sons and your wives, and on all that you own,

L.14: look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is about to strike a great blow on your people and on your sons and on your wives and on all your possessions,

R.14: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is going to send a terrible disaster on your people, your sons, your wives and everything you own.

decisions.choice: look ... is about to strike: the result of what Jehoram has done
decisions.reason: After the charge ("because ...", verses 12-13) comes the sentence. "Look" with the participle announces something about to happen.

decisions.choice: a great blow: a disaster sent by Yahweh
decisions.reason: The word can mean a plague, but it is used of any blow Yahweh strikes, including defeat in war (1 Samuel 4:17). Verses 16-17 tell how it fell: raiders carried off the king's goods, sons and wives.

decisions.choice: so now (Balanced); So (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the link between the charge and the sentence with "so" in place of "look".

decisions.choice: a terrible disaster
decisions.reason: Readable says "disaster", which covers both the raid and the loss it brings (m2).

records.source: וְאַתָּ֛ה בָּחֳלָיִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים בְּמַחֲלֵ֣ה מֵעֶ֑יךָ עַד־יֵצְא֤וּ מֵעֶ֨יךָ֙ מִן־הַחֹ֔לִי יָמִ֖ים עַל־יָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: and you [will be] with sicknesses many, with sickness of your bowels, until come out your bowels from the sickness days upon days.
pieces: and you yourself will suffer severe illness, with a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the disease, day after day."

L.15: and you [will be] in many sicknesses, with a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out from the disease, days upon days."

R.15: And you yourself will become very sick with a disease in your bowels. The disease will go on day after day, until your bowels come out because of it."

decisions.choice: a disease of the bowels
decisions.reason: The bowels are the intestines and inner organs. The disease cannot be named with certainty; it was long and painful, and ended with the bowels coming out (verse 19).

decisions.choice: days upon days: over a long time, day after day
alternatives: after some time (the bowels came out after a long illness)
decisions.reason: The phrase means that the illness would go on and grow worse over time. Verse 19 says it lasted two years.

decisions.choice: and you: judgment on the king himself
decisions.reason: After the blow on his household (verse 14), the sentence turns to Jehoram himself, with an emphatic "you". The letter ends here; verses 16-19 tell how both parts came true.

decisions.choice: you yourself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "you yourself" to keep the stress of the Hebrew pronoun (m3).

records.source: וַיָּ֨עַר יְהוָ֜ה עַל־יְהוֹרָ֗ם אֵ֣ת ר֤וּחַ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ וְהָ֣עַרְבִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־יַ֥ד כּוּשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And stirred up Yahweh against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabs who [were] at [the] hand of [the] Cushites.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stirred up the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Cushites against Jehoram.

L.16: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and the Arabs who [were] beside the Cushites.

R.16: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made the Philistines and the Arabs who lived near the Cushites want to attack Jehoram.

decisions.choice: stirred up the spirit: moved them to act
decisions.reason: To stir up someone's spirit is to move him to do something, as Yahweh stirred up the spirit of the king of Assyria (1 Chronicles 5:26) and of Cyrus (36:22). Here Yahweh uses foreign peoples to carry out the blow of verse 14.

decisions.choice: the Arabs who were beside the Cushites
decisions.reason: "At the hand of" means "next to". These Cushites were probably a people living south of Judah, near Gerar, like Zerah's army in 14:8-14, rather than the Cush of the upper Nile. The Philistines and Arabs had brought gifts to Jehoshaphat (17:11); now they turn against his son.

decisions.choice: stirred up the Philistines (Balanced); made ... want to attack (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced folds "the spirit of" into the verb, since stirring up a people means stirring up their will. Readable says what they were stirred up to do.

records.source: וַיַּעֲל֤וּ בִֽיהוּדָה֙ וַיִּבְקָע֔וּהָ וַיִּשְׁבּ֗וּ אֵ֤ת כָּל־הָרְכוּשׁ֙ הַנִּמְצָ֣א לְבֵית־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְגַם־בָּנָ֖יו וְנָשָׁ֑יו וְלֹ֤א נִשְׁאַר־לוֹ֙ בֵּ֔ן כִּ֥י אִם־יְהוֹאָחָ֖ז קְטֹ֥ן בָּנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And they came up against Judah and broke into it, and they carried away all the possessions found in [the] house of the king, and also his sons and his wives; and not was left to him a son except Jehoahaz, [the] youngest of his sons.
pieces: They came up against Judah and broke into it. They took away as plunder all the goods they found in the king's palace, and his sons and wives as well. Not one son was left to him except Jehoahaz, his youngest.

L.17: And they came up against Judah and broke into it, and they carried away all the possessions that were found in the king's house, and also his sons and his wives; and no son was left to him except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.

R.17: They attacked Judah and broke through its defenses. They carried away everything of value in the king's palace, and they took his sons and his wives too. The only son left to him was Jehoahaz, the youngest.

decisions.choice: broke into it: broke through Judah's defenses
decisions.reason: The verb means to split or break open, used of breaking through a wall or a line (2 Kings 25:4). The raiders forced their way into the land.

decisions.choice: the king's house: the palace, and perhaps the king's household
decisions.reason: The house of the king is his palace. The raid may not have reached Jerusalem itself: the goods, sons and wives may have been those at the king's residences elsewhere. 22:1 says the raiders killed all the older sons.

decisions.choice: Jehoahaz: the son who reigned as Ahaziah
decisions.reason: 22:1 calls the youngest son Ahaziah, as 2 Kings 8:24 does. Both names are made of the same two parts, "Yahweh" and "has grasped", in the opposite order. It is one person.

decisions.choice: the first part of the letter comes true
decisions.reason: The blow on his people, sons, wives and possessions (verse 14) falls as foretold.

decisions.choice: palace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "palace" for the king's house.

records.source: וְאַחֲרֵ֖י כָּל־זֹ֑את נְגָפ֨וֹ יְהוָ֧ה׀בְּמֵעָ֛יו לָחֳלִ֖י לְאֵ֥ין מַרְפֵּֽא׃
records.gloss: And after all this struck him Yahweh in his bowels with a sickness for which there [was] no healing.
pieces: After all this {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck him with an incurable disease of the bowels.

L.18: And after all this {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck him in his bowels with a disease for which there [was] no healing.

R.18: After all this, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck Jehoram with a disease in his bowels that could not be cured.

decisions.choice: the second part of the letter comes true
decisions.reason: The disease of the bowels foretold in verse 15 now strikes him.

decisions.choice: no healing: no cure
decisions.reason: The word means healing or remedy. The disease was beyond any cure.

decisions.choice: Jehoram
decisions.reason: Readable names Jehoram for "him".

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י לְיָמִ֣ים׀מִיָּמִ֡ים וּכְעֵת֩ צֵ֨את הַקֵּ֜ץ לְיָמִ֣ים שְׁנַ֗יִם יָצְא֤וּ מֵעָיו֙ עִם־חָלְי֔וֹ וַיָּ֖מָת בְּתַחֲלֻאִ֣ים רָעִ֑ים וְלֹא־עָ֨שׂוּ ל֥וֹ עַמּ֛וֹ שְׂרֵפָ֖ה כִּשְׂרֵפַ֥ת אֲבֹתָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And it was, at days from days, and at [the] time of [the] going out of the end, at days two [years], came out his bowels with his sickness, and he died in harmful diseases; and not made for him his people a burning like [the] burning of his fathers.
pieces: In the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of his disease, and he died in great pain. His people made no fire in his honor like the fire made for his ancestors.

L.19: And it happened in the course of days, and at the time of the coming of the end, after two years, his bowels came out with his disease, and he died in terrible pains. And his people did not make a burning for him like the burning of his fathers.

R.19: As time passed, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of the disease, and he died in terrible pain. His people did not light a fire to honor him, as they had done for the kings before him.

decisions.choice: in the course of days ... at the end of two years
decisions.reason: The first phrase means "as time went on"; the second dates the end of his illness two years after it began. The words of verse 15 come true.

decisions.choice: a burning: a great fire in honor of the dead king, as for Asa
decisions.reason: At Asa's burial "they made a very great burning for him" (16:14), with spices. Such a fire honored a king (Jeremiah 34:5); the king's body was not burned. Jehoram was denied it.

decisions.choice: harmful diseases: severe sufferings
decisions.reason: The word for diseases is plural and means painful sicknesses or sufferings; with "harmful" it describes a death in great pain.

decisions.choice: his fathers: the kings before him
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means his royal forefathers.

decisions.choice: fire in his honor (Balanced); light a fire to honor him (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "fire" for "burning" and add that it was to honor him (m2). Readable says "the kings before him" for "his fathers".

records.source: בֶּן־שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וּשְׁמוֹנֶ֣ה שָׁנִ֔ים מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ בְּלֹ֣א חֶמְדָּ֔ה וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֨הוּ֙ בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֔יד וְלֹ֖א בְּקִבְר֥וֹת הַמְּלָכִֽים׃
records.gloss: A son of thirty and two he was when he became king, and eight years he reigned in Jerusalem; and he went with no regret, and they buried him in [the] city of David, but not in [the] tombs of the kings.
pieces: He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He departed with no one's regret. They buried him in the City of David, but not in the royal tombs.

L.20: He was a son of thirty-two when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. And he departed with no regret, and they buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

R.20: He became king at the age of thirty-two, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eight years. When he died, no one was sorry. He was buried in the City of David, but not in the place where the kings were buried.

decisions.choice: the accession formula of verse 5, repeated
decisions.reason: The verse repeats verse 5 to close Jehoram's reign, as Chronicles sometimes does (27:1, 8).

decisions.choice: he departed with no regret: he died and no one missed him
decisions.reason: "He went" means he died. "Without desire" means no one held him dear or longed for him: no one mourned his death.

decisions.choice: buried in the City of David but not in the tombs of the kings
decisions.reason: Burial apart from the royal tombs was a mark of dishonor, as for Joash (24:25) and Uzziah (26:23). 2 Kings 8:24 says he was buried "with his fathers in the City of David"; Chronicles adds that it was not in the kings' tombs.

decisions.choice: they buried him: his people buried him
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it means that he was buried, by his people (verse 19).

decisions.choice: departed with no one's regret (Balanced); no one was sorry (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "departed" for "went" and says whose regret is missing; Readable says plainly that he died and no one was sorry.
